walkthrough.title: Triage suicide screen (ASQ)
walkthrough.notes: 28-year-old presents to a general medical ED with severe insomnia and anxiety; chronic pain and recent job loss. Triage-time ASQ administered and captured as discrete data.

walkthrough.title: Derived risk tier — non-acute positive
walkthrough.notes: Screen classified as non-acute positive (wish to be dead + thoughts of suicide, no current ideation/plan). Risk tier surfaced on the trackboard.

walkthrough.title: Suicide-screening-status flag raised
walkthrough.notes: Suicide-screening-status flag set so the positive screen is visible across the care team and downstream views.

walkthrough.title: Role-routed task: BH consult / brief assessment
walkthrough.notes: Positive screen fires the Identify Possible Risk → Clarify Risk transition: a role-routed task and behavioral-health consult request are generated from the pathway PlanDefinition.

walkthrough.title: Mitigation checklist — patient relocated to safe room
walkthrough.notes: Environmental-safety mitigation checklist completed; patient moved to a ligature-resistant room.

walkthrough.title: Suicide-precautions order signed
walkthrough.notes: Observation-level suicide precautions ordered with required provider signature.

walkthrough.title: Room cleared + belongings secured
walkthrough.notes: Room clearance checklist documented; personal belongings inventoried and secured.

walkthrough.title: Continuous 1:1 observation started
walkthrough.notes: 1:1 continuous observation initiated with time-stamped observation log and a documented observer assignment.

walkthrough.title: Brief Suicide Safety Assessment (BSSA)
walkthrough.notes: BSSA performed after the positive ASQ to clarify whether a full risk assessment is needed. (Tool TL-005 is planned — not yet a built SPiER Questionnaire.)

walkthrough.title: BSSA outcome recorded and next step routed
walkthrough.notes: The BSSA determination is persisted as discrete data and routes the next stage rather than living in a note: a full risk assessment is ordered before any disposition decision, which is why 11.4-1A follows. The "cannot leave until evaluated" hold was deliberately not applied — Maria screened non-acute positive, and that status is reserved for acute presentations. The determination carries text rather than a code: no LOINC concept exists for a BSSA routing decision, and this step is marked as a profile gap for exactly that reason.

walkthrough.title: Full risk assessment — C-SSRS Full + SAFE-T framing
walkthrough.notes: Full risk assessment completed using the C-SSRS Full (Lifetime/Recent) within a SAFE-T framing. (C-SSRS Full is built; SAFE-T framing TL-006 is planned.)

walkthrough.title: Current risk level set (high) + risk condition coded
walkthrough.notes: Current suicide risk level set to high; a coded suicide-risk Condition and a longitudinal risk Flag are persisted.

walkthrough.title: Boarding reassessment cadence scheduled
walkthrough.notes: Patient boards in the ED awaiting an inpatient bed; a time-based reassessment cadence is scheduled from the reassessment PlanDefinition.

walkthrough.title: Reassessment — risk updated, precautions maintained
walkthrough.notes: Scheduled reassessment performed; updated risk recorded and precautions maintained, preserving prior values.

walkthrough.title: Collaborative Stanley-Brown safety plan
walkthrough.notes: Collaborative Stanley-Brown safety plan completed with the patient and stored as a CarePlan.

walkthrough.title: Safety plan versioned + provenance
walkthrough.notes: Safety plan retained with version history and Provenance for each revision.

walkthrough.title: Patient reviews and accepts the safety plan
walkthrough.notes: Maria revised two warning signs into her own words, agreed her sister could be named as a support and contacted, and declined naming her employer. The decline is recorded rather than dropped, so the outpatient team knows it was discussed.

walkthrough.title: Lethal-means counseling delivered
walkthrough.notes: Lethal-means counseling delivered and documented; means-safety actions (who/what/when/where) added to the care plan. Recorded with TL-008, which is built: the counseling Procedure and the per-method means-safety Observations are what its recorder writes.

walkthrough.title: Discharge-readiness checklist (gating)
walkthrough.notes: Discharge readiness checklist completed; a blocking alert would have prevented discharge until safety planning and means counseling were on file.

walkthrough.title: Patient and sister commit to means-safety actions
walkthrough.notes: Two time-bound actions agreed: the sister takes the stored medication home the same evening, and the patient moves the remaining supply to a lock box within 48 hours. Each has a named owner and a due date rather than being recorded only as counseling delivered.

walkthrough.title: After-visit summary + safety plan to patient
walkthrough.notes: Suicide-specific after-visit summary generated; printed/portal-delivered safety plan and discharge instructions provided to the patient.

walkthrough.title: Release rules applied before portal delivery
walkthrough.notes: The after-visit packet reached the portal only after checking who could see it. No proxy access is configured on this adult record, so the safety plan released in full — and the rule that produced that decision is recorded alongside it, rather than the release being simply automatic.

walkthrough.title: Disclosure authorization captured before the packet
walkthrough.actor: ED Clinician / Consent and Privacy Manager
walkthrough.notes: Maria authorized sending the risk summary, safety plan and follow-up plan to the named outpatient BH program, for this episode only. She is an adult and no 42 CFR Part 2 program is involved, so no emergency exception was relied on. Recorded before 11.7-1B assembled the packet.

walkthrough.title: Urgent outpatient BH referral + appointment request
walkthrough.notes: Urgent outpatient behavioral-health referral placed with an appointment request and a communication to the receiving provider. (Tool TL-009 is planned.)

walkthrough.title: Transition-of-care packet transmitted
walkthrough.notes: Suicide-specific transition-of-care packet (safety plan + risk summary + follow-up plan) transmitted to outpatient BH, with Provenance for delivery.

walkthrough.title: Confirm outpatient receipt of packet
walkthrough.notes: Awaiting confirmation that the receiving outpatient BH program received the transition packet and scheduled the appointment.

walkthrough.title: 24–48h follow-up outreach call scheduled
walkthrough.notes: First follow-up outreach call (24–48h post-discharge) scheduled per the follow-up PlanDefinition, together with registry enrollment for the caring contact that follows in 11.7-2B. (Tools TL-010 / TL-033 are planned.)

walkthrough.title: Patient answers the 48-hour caring contact
walkthrough.notes: Maria answered the 48-hour call, reported using two coping strategies from the plan, and asked to be reached by text rather than phone in future. The channel change is recorded as a preference update, not as a refusal of contact.

walkthrough.title: 7-day caring contact + risk recheck
walkthrough.notes: 7-day caring contact — a brief, non-demanding note asking nothing in return — with an updated risk check and care-plan review.

walkthrough.title: Overdue-follow-up escalation guard
walkthrough.notes: If a follow-up attempt is missed, the task transitions to overdue and a supervisor alert plus an escalated follow-up Flag fire automatically.

tasks.description: Full suicide risk assessment (C-SSRS Full within SAFE-T framing) before a disposition decision — routed from the BSSA determination.
